ideas.risks: The audit may confirm the current obstruction: existing boosters either require tunable weak advantage, distribution-specific smoothness parameters, or exponential dependence on a weak sample/capacity parameter.
ideas.summary: Audit agnostic boosting theorems for the exact oracle model: a distribution-free learner with fixed additive excess beta, improper binary output, and representation-uniform polynomial running time. For each candidate theorem, write the precise weak learner condition, runtime dependence on epsilon, gamma, VC/capacity, and whether the weak call is only required when OPT_C < gamma.
ideas.title: Exact Agnostic Boosting Audit
ideas.why_promising: The edge may already be settled by a theorem whose assumptions are close but easy to misread. Even a negative audit would isolate the exact missing condition for later attacks.

ideas.risks: This would only refute black-box reductions, not the atlas implication, because a real reduction may exploit representation-specific structure or the code of A.
ideas.summary: Formalize a black-box lower bound where the weak learner oracle is adversarial but satisfies the fixed-slack guarantee. Use a hidden clean component of mass 1 - 2 eta with eta in the hard band gamma <= eta <= 1/2 - epsilon, and make all polynomially many queried distributions have OPT_C >= gamma unless they identify the hidden component.
ideas.title: Adversarial Weak-Oracle Barrier
ideas.why_promising: The solver attempt already identifies clean-witness generation as the bottleneck. A rigorous oracle barrier would convert that intuition into a precise obstruction and prevent wasted effort on purely black-box boosters.

ideas.risks: Validation may not certify that a hypothesis useful on a clean slice helps on the original distribution; the enumeration may still be polynomial only under very strong sample-size or compression assumptions.
ideas.summary: Investigate a conditional positive theorem under a small-sample or sample-compression assumption on A. If A uses k examples or has compression size k = O(log poly(1/epsilon)), enumerate candidate training subsets from a larger sample, run A on each induced empirical distribution, and use held-out validation plus boosting to select useful hypotheses.
ideas.title: Compression-Based Clean Witnesses
ideas.why_promising: It directly attacks the exponential clean-batch probability in the solver attempt. The condition is concrete, checkable, and may yield a clean theorem even if the unrestricted edge remains open.

ideas.risks: Natural code classes may fail the source guarantee because low-noise weighted distribution-free decoding is already hard; conversely, any decoder strong enough for all distributions may imply stronger approximate decoding.
ideas.summary: Search for a represented Boolean class induced by codewords where fixed low-radius weighted decoding is efficient but moderate-noise approximate decoding is hard. Translate arbitrary example distributions into coordinate weights and ask whether unique decoding below gamma can coexist with hardness of achieving eta + epsilon under random classification noise eta > gamma.
ideas.title: Code-Like Separation Candidate
ideas.why_promising: The solver gives a crisp conditional separation recipe. Coding theory is the most natural place to look for a gap between low-noise recovery and moderate-noise recovery.

ideas.risks: Binary labels and bounded correlations may prevent any amplification strong enough to overcome the fixed additive slack; the transformation may require knowing or approximating the optimal comparator already.
ideas.summary: Try to construct residual-label transformations that force OPT_C below gamma whenever the current aggregate hypothesis has excess error above epsilon. The explorer should define the transformed distribution explicitly from observable samples and the current predictor, then prove or refute that some comparator in C has low error on it.
ideas.title: Residual Forcing Without Clean Labels
ideas.why_promising: A successful lemma would bypass hidden clean-subset enumeration and give a genuine boosting route. A failed formalization would sharpen why fixed slack differs from ordinary agnostic weak advantage.

ideas.risks: SQ access alone may not overcome constant additive slack; known SQ boosting results may still require a tunable weak learner or tolerances that deteriorate with epsilon.
ideas.summary: Assume A is implementable by statistical queries, or is stable under reweighting, and test whether standard agnostic boosting can be made representation-uniform. The target is a theorem of the form: fixed-slack weak agnostic learning plus SQ/stability/smoothness implies agnostic improper learning with polynomial dependence on 1/epsilon.
ideas.title: SQ Or Stability Assumptions
ideas.why_promising: The solver flags extra assumptions on A as plausible. SQ and stability are natural restrictions that might turn hidden clean structure into estimable residual correlations.

ideas.risks: An anchor may let the oracle satisfy its guarantee by solving only the easy part, so it could hide the target signal instead of amplifying it.
ideas.summary: Explore whether mixing the target distribution with an easy known realizable anchor distribution can force useful behavior from A. Precisely quantify how large the target residual mass must be before a fixed beta slack oracle cannot ignore it; if impossible, prove an anchor-doping no-go lemma.
ideas.title: Anchor Doping And Signal Amplification
ideas.why_promising: This tests a common way to convert weak constant-accuracy oracles into useful subroutines. Either outcome would be informative: a construction gives a new route, while a no-go explains another obstruction.

ideas.risks: Finite experiments can mislead because computational hardness and representation-uniformity are asymptotic; they may only find oracle artifacts.
ideas.summary: Build finite-domain LP/minimax models for small X and C. Model the weak oracle as any response satisfying err <= OPT_C + beta, then ask whether a meta-algorithm with bounded calls can force an OPT_C + epsilon hypothesis. Search for minimal hard instances and inspect their geometry.
ideas.title: Finite Minimax Testbed
ideas.why_promising: Small exact instances can reveal whether the obstruction is geometric, oracle-theoretic, or merely computational. They can also generate candidate counterexamples for formalization.

ideas.risks: Such a result may be too narrow for the atlas edge, and some noise assumptions make the original weak learner trivially informative only below gamma, not enough for strong accuracy.
ideas.summary: Look for positive results under natural noise restrictions, such as Massart noise with rate bounded away from 1/2, Tsybakov conditions, or eta < gamma on all relevant reweighted residual distributions. State exactly which condition makes fixed-slack calls informative throughout boosting.
ideas.title: Noise-Restricted Positive Route
ideas.why_promising: The run goals allow conditional theorems. A precise noise-model theorem could separate what fails in fully agnostic learning from what survives under structured noise.
